tokens.title: Access tokens
tokens.description: With an access token, an AI client such as Claude Code or Codex reads and works over MCP on your behalf: never with more rights than you, only in the token's spaces, and everything it writes carries the AI mark with the token's name.
tokens.empty: You have no access token yet.

profile.title: Access tokens for AI clients
profile.text: Connect Claude Code, Codex or another MCP client to this installation.

create.title: Create access token
create.hint: Best with only the spaces and the mode the client needs.
create.agentHint: The token acts as this agent, with at most its responsible person's rights and only in its spaces.

fields.name: Name
fields.nameHint: How you will recognise it, e.g. “Claude Code laptop”.
fields.daysHint: 1 to {{max}} days; after that the token stops working.

explain.read: Search and read: pages, tickets, spaces (never drafts).
explain.write: Also create and comment on tickets, status up to “In review”, page proposals and messages in channels.

agentExplain.read: Search, read and see its own tickets.
agentExplain.write: Also pick up and comment on tickets, status up to “In review” and page proposals, as far as its level and grants allow.

scope.required: Please choose at least one space.

secret.title: Your new token: {{name}}
secret.description: Copy it now and connect your client.
secret.warning: The token is shown this once and stored nowhere. If it is lost, you can only revoke it and create a new one. Whoever has it acts as you within its scope.
secret.label: Token

connect.title: Connect a client
connect.variable: Put the token into the environment variable {{variable}}, never into a checked-in file and never into an address. Then:
connect.agentTask: A good task for the agent: “Call list_my_tickets, take the first ticket with claim_ticket, work on it, comment on the result and set it to ‘In review’.”

calls.hint: The latest tool calls over /mcp, newest first. No content is stored.

revoke.title: Revoke token?
revoke.text: “{{name}}” stops working at once; every client that uses it loses access. This cannot be undone.

admin.description: External AI clients such as Claude Code or Codex read and work over /mcp with access tokens, never with more rights than their person.

settings.title: Access over MCP
settings.hint: One switch for the whole organisation; every change is in the audit log.
settings.enabledHint: Every active member except guests (and people with “no AI”) may create their own access tokens. Off: every token answers as unknown until switched on again.
settings.on: On: every active member except guests may create access tokens.
settings.off: Off: nobody can create or use access tokens.
settings.locationHint: For the spaces' AI policy a client counts as a connection with this data location: spaces that do not allow it cannot be read through tokens. “External” as long as the clients do not run in-house.

admin.tokensHint: Name and metadata only; nobody knows a token's clear text. Revoking also works while access is off.
admin.empty: Nobody has created a token yet.

token.not_found: This token does not exist (any more).
token.space_invalid: You may not read one of the spaces (any more). Choose the spaces again.
token.agent_not_external: Tokens exist only for external agents.
token.responsible_without_mcp: The agent's responsible person may not hold access tokens (MCP switched off, no AI or not active).
